capabilities.title: What it does
capabilities.subtitle: The assistant is the part people see. The advantage is everything sitting behind it.

items.title: Agents that do the work
items.body: Multi-step jobs that pull a report together, watch for something changing, or send a summary on — run on a schedule or a trigger. Each agent has its own skills, its own memory, and a ceiling it cannot spend past. A step that fails for a moment tries again; a step that sends or changes something outside Hakken only ever gets one try.

items.title: Private company knowledge
items.body: Documents, uploads and company guidance stay inside the right workspace. Search matches both the words people used and what they meant, so an answer is not missed because somebody phrased it differently.
tags: Upload a folder at a time

items.title: A person in the loop
items.body: Before an agent writes, sends or changes anything outside Hakken it stops and waits. You set how much rope each agent gets. Waiting work sits in one queue somebody owns, and an unanswered request expires rather than hanging there forever.
tags: You set how far it can go
One queue for what is waiting

items.title: Never tied to one AI company
items.body: Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter all sit behind one screen. If one of them changes their prices, you switch — you do not rebuild.

items.title: Customer-facing widgets
items.body: Branded assistants for a website or portal, testable safely before a customer ever sees one.

items.title: Spend that cannot run away
items.body: Every run carries a hard ceiling on steps, tool calls, minutes and money, and stops when it reaches it.

safety.title: Every message is checked before the AI acts on it
safety.subtitle: People will try to talk your AI into things, and they will paste personal details into it without thinking. Both are handled before a single tool runs — here is a real one arriving.
safety.note: Nothing here reached a model with its instructions intact, and nothing a person would not want written down was written down.

gates.title: Hidden instructions
gates.body: Attempts to get at the system prompt, tool list or private configuration are caught by their shape, not a banned word list.

gates.title: Talking past the rules
gates.body: “Ignore previous instructions”, “disable safety rules”, “bypass permissions” — the whole family, in whatever wording it arrives.

gates.title: Reaching into another company
gates.body: Asking for another client's documents, users or history is stopped at the door, on top of the separation already in the data.

gates.title: Personal details removed
gates.body: Card numbers, emails and phone numbers are stripped before anything is stored — from chat history and from what agents record doing.

learning.title: It gets better at the job without anybody retraining it
learning.subtitle: Four loops run continuously. Two of them change nothing anyone believes, so they run on their own. The two that would teach the AI something new always stop and ask.

steps.name: Reflect
steps.title: Every run that went wrong is looked at
steps.body: A failed or awkward run is examined for why, and what would have avoided it becomes a suggestion rather than a lost afternoon.

steps.name: Rank
steps.title: What it already knows gets reordered by what worked
steps.body: Documents and memories that keep producing good answers rise; ones that never help sink. Nothing new is believed, so nobody has to sign this off.

steps.name: Listen
steps.title: A thumbs-down is a signal, not a shrug
steps.body: Ratings from your own team and from customers using your widgets feed straight back in, instead of sitting in a table nobody opens.

steps.name: Learn
steps.title: New facts about your company queue up for a person
steps.body: Live conversations propose things worth remembering. They wait in a queue until somebody says yes, because this is the loop that changes what the AI tells people.

control.title: What you control

items.title: Every company kept apart
items.body: Companies, people, documents, chat history, settings and permissions each sit in their own workspace rather than one shared pool.

items.title: Roles that mean something
items.body: Platform owners, company managers and everyday users each get their own screens and their own limits — which is what lets you sell the same product to several companies at once.

items.title: Nothing the AI does is open-ended
items.body: Every tool is set up deliberately, given permission and recorded. It only runs down approved paths.

items.title: History you can read, and clear
items.body: Settings changes, conversations, AI activity, finished flows and failed ones are all there to inspect. Separate clean-up schedules decide how long each kind is kept, and you turn each one on yourself.

items.title: Told when something breaks
items.body: Stuck runs, unanswered approvals, failing tools and cost pressure are watched, and you get emailed rather than having to remember to look.

items.title: Everyone who has ever signed in
items.body: One list of every person on the platform, when they last signed in and how often — sortable, without giving anybody a button that changes a user.

governance.title: The paperwork answers itself
governance.subtitle: The questions a buyer's legal team asks — what AI is running, who signed it off, what happens if it goes wrong, what do you hold about me — have answers the platform keeps on its own, rather than a document somebody writes the week before the audit.

points.title: A register that fills itself
points.body: Every agent, model and tool in use is listed as it is created, not remembered later.

points.title: The rules in force, in one list
points.body: Everything currently constraining what the AI may do, readable in one place instead of scattered across settings.

points.title: A risk rating that actually restrains
points.body: Rating something high risk changes what it is allowed to do. It is not a label on a spreadsheet.

points.title: An auditor can look, and change nothing
points.body: They get their own sign-in that reaches the evidence and no other part of the platform.

points.title: “What do you hold about me?”
points.body: A person can be answered in full, and deleted in full, without an engineer writing a query.

points.title: The evidence pack, written to be read

points.title: Your customers get the same view

proof.title: How you know the AI does the right thing
proof.subtitle: AI products fail quietly. Permissions drift, actions reach too far, a prompt gets attacked and a journey breaks with nobody watching. Four things stand in the way of that.

items.title: Graded AI checks
items.body: A check is a task and a description of a good result. Running one gives the task to the real agent, with its real tools and documents, and a second AI marks what came back.

items.title: A full rehearsal
items.body: The agent runs the whole job for real — real documents, real tools, real decisions — with anything it would have sent or changed recorded instead of done. Then it gets marked.

items.title: It cannot go live until its checks pass
items.body: You choose which checks have to pass before an agent can be switched on. Until they do, it stays a draft, however much anyone wants to ship it.

items.title: A timeline of what it actually did
items.body: What it was asked, which tools it called, what came back, where it stopped and what it cost. Failed runs can be replayed rather than guessed at.

engineering.title: Built to a standard you can check
engineering.subtitle: Anyone can demo an AI product. What a serious buyer wants to know is what happens on the day it breaks, and whether the team that built it left anything behind. Those answers are all countable.

figures.label: Automated tests, run on every single change
Separate test files across the platform
Whole customer journeys driven through a real browser
Written guides for developers, operators and end users

items.title: Keeping companies apart is tested, not assumed
items.body: A standing set of tests tries to reach one company's documents, users and history from inside another, and has to fail every time. Sign-in, roles, prompt attacks and personal-data handling are held to the same standard.

items.title: Nothing lands unless everything is green
items.body: Every change runs the full suite plus type and code checks before it can go in. A test that starts failing stops the change, not the release.

items.title: Test coverage has a floor it cannot fall through
items.body: How much of the code the tests actually cover is recorded, and a change that drops it below that level is rejected. The number can go up, and never quietly down.

items.title: Written down for whoever has to run it
items.body: Three separate sets of documentation: for the team building on the platform, the team operating it, and the people using it day to day. Not one README and a hope.

firstPerson.controls: WASD move · Mouse look · Q/E turn · Space decoy dash · Esc pause · M map

courtyard.name: Lantern Courtyard
courtyard.description: Slip through the lantern-lit courtyard. Recover three stolen seals, misdirect the patrols, and reach the eastern gate.

market.name: Night Market
market.description: Weave between silk stalls and lantern alleys. Choose your route carefully — guards patrol the crossings.

docks.name: Canal Docks
docks.description: Cross the moonlit quays and three timber bridges. Mechanical hounds track your trail along the water.

gardens.name: Fortress Gardens
gardens.description: One final heist. Circle the fortress gardens, recover the last seals, and slip through the great gate.

billingAdmin.title: Billing
billingAdmin.description: Manage subscriptions, Stripe setup and customer billing across your product.
billingAdmin.restricted: Platform billing is available only to super admins outside company impersonation.
billingAdmin.overviewDescription: See paying companies, the users their subscriptions cover and accounts that need attention.
billingAdmin.failed: Billing could not be loaded or saved. Please retry.
billingAdmin.calculating: Calculating totals across all companies and users…
billingAdmin.reportTime: Report completed {date} · {mode}. Refresh to include subsequent changes.
billingAdmin.metricDefinition: Paying companies have a confirmed paid period that has not expired. Users are registered company members and company admins, excluding anonymous and platform roles. Grace-only access is excluded. Monthly value includes subscriptions until their paid period ends; it is before taxes, refunds and fees, and is not collected revenue. Totals are a dated report across successive reads.
billingAdmin.stale: {count} billing accounts have not synced successfully in the last 30 minutes. Review Stripe before relying on these totals.
billingAdmin.companiesDescription: Find any company, including companies with an operator-managed plan or no subscription.
billingAdmin.setupDescription: Connect this product to its Stripe account, link prices and enable company self-service.
billingAdmin.credentialsHelp: Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in this deployment’s Convex environment. Credentials stay on the server and are never shown here.
billingAdmin.keyMissing: Stripe key missing or wrong mode
billingAdmin.webhookHelp: Add this endpoint in Stripe using API version 2026-05-27.dahlia. Subscribe to checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.expired, customer.subscription.created, customer.subscription.updated, customer.subscription.deleted, invoice.paid and invoice.payment_failed.
billingAdmin.noWebhook: No verified webhook received yet. Configured credentials alone do not prove delivery.
billingAdmin.modeLocked: Billing accounts already exist. Use a separate deployment to switch between test and live billing.
billingAdmin.graceHelp: 0–30 days of temporary access after a previously paid subscription becomes past due. This does not count as a paid period.
billingAdmin.enableHelp: Company admins can subscribe and manage billing in the normal user frontend. Existing subscribers must retain access to billing; retire plans to stop selling them.
billingAdmin.portalHelp: When billing is enabled, saving verifies the linked monthly prices and creates matching Stripe portal profiles for plan changes and payment recovery. Payment methods, invoices and cancellation stay with Stripe.
billingAdmin.liveHelp: Saving with live billing enabled makes these plans available for real customer payments.
billingAdmin.priceHelp: Create fixed monthly prices in Stripe, then choose one here. The server verifies the amount, currency and product. Linking a new price changes future offers; existing subscriptions keep their agreed price until changed through Stripe. Supported currencies: GBP, EUR and USD.
billingAdmin.noPrices: No supported prices on the loaded pages. Create an active fixed monthly price in Stripe.
billingAdmin.inactivePlan: Activate this plan before linking a price. Existing subscribers can still use payment recovery after a plan is retired.
billingAdmin.stripeManaged: Stripe manages this subscription. Change its plan in Stripe; the company’s entitlements follow confirmed payment.
